title: Compounding NFT mint price growth in NFTMinterV2._executeMint is monotonic but accelerates super-linearly; cap and overflow analysis assumes 18-decimal token and bounded growthBasisPoints
description:
Acknowledged as a known-design feature (per the audit prompt). The line `config.price = price + (price * config.growthBasisPoints) / 10000;` compounds price every mint. There is no upper bound on growthBasisPoints (`setGrowthFactor` accepts any uint256). Two minor concerns:

  1. With growthBasisPoints == 10000 (100%), price doubles every mint. Starting from 1e18 (1 token), after 256 mints price > 2^256 and the multiplication `price * growthBasisPoints` overflows uint256. Solidity 0.8.20 reverts on overflow, so the mint reverts cleanly — no silent corruption. But this means a misconfigured high growthBasisPoints turns the dispatcher into a bricked-after-N-mints state.

  2. With growthBasisPoints == 0, price stays flat (no growth) — that's a documented escape.

  3. With sane growthBasisPoints (e.g., 100 = 1%), price grows ~e^(0.01 * n) after n mints. After 1000 mints price has grown by a factor of e^10 ~ 22,000x. If the dispatcher's price starts at 100 USDS this becomes 2.2M USDS per mint — effectively closing the dispatcher organically. This is the intended design but is worth confirming the off-chain UI handles this gracefully (e.g., displays the next price prominently and front-end users do not mistakenly approve an unbounded ERC20 amount).

No arithmetic bug was found within the formula itself. The math is exact under Solidity 0.8 overflow checks.
exploit_path: No direct exploit. Possible UX trap: a user pre-approves a large allowance to NFTMinterV2 expecting to pay the current price, then mints later when price has grown — paying the new (higher) price up to allowance. This is standard ERC20-approval semantics and not a contract-level bug, but the compounding price magnifies the surprise. A malicious frontrunner could observe a pending mint and have other minters race in to push the price up, forcing the original minter to pay more than expected (or revert if allowance is exhausted).
mainnet_realism: Pure on-chain logic. No Balancer dependency.
recommendation: (1) Cap growthBasisPoints in setGrowthFactor (e.g., require <= 10000 for sanity). (2) Document the compounding behaviour prominently in front-end UX and require minters to specify a maxPrice on mint (front-run protection). (3) Consider rate-limiting price growth so multiple mints in one block do not all compound (e.g., growth applies once per block, or once per N minutes), reducing front-run/sandwich exposure on the mint itself.
oos_reason: Known issue KI #6: 'Price growth via basis points may compound to very large values over many mints (documented design).' Finding explicitly acknowledges this is known-design (per the audit prompt) and does not identify a novel arithmetic bug or a new attack vector beyond the documented compounding behavior.
